metadata.description: Self-hosted best-practice plugins: UI/UX stacks, frameworks, game engines, databases, architecture, design patterns, testing, security, API design, dev environments, and the taskmaster clarification-to-execution workflow suite.

plugins.name: ui-ux
plugins.description: UI/UX foundations with per-stack skills for shadcn/ui and Tailwind, a design-tokens skill (spacing/type/radius/elevation/motion scales + semantic color tiering), a theming-system skill, motion best practices, theme creation with a live colour preview, a /ui-ux:build entry point, a WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility audit (/ui-ux:audit, the a11y-audit skill, and an a11y-engineer worker), and ui-ux-reviewer + ui-ux-engineer agents. Component-library skills (MUI, Astryx, ReUI, Aceternity, PrimeReact, component-libraries) live in the ui-libraries plugin — install both.

plugins.name: ui-libraries
plugins.description: Component-library skills split out of ui-ux: Material UI (with MUI X), PrimeReact (v11 rewrite and licence), Astryx, ReUI, Aceternity UI, and a library-agnostic component-libraries skill with a per-library map of signals, theme channels and docs for every other React or Vue library (Base UI, Radix, React Aria, Ark, Mantine, Chakra, Ant Design, HeroUI, PrimeVue, Vuetify…). Install alongside ui-ux, which owns shadcn, Tailwind, theming, tokens, motion and the WCAG audit.

plugins.name: craft-layer
plugins.description: Create unique, animated, informative web apps (CRM, SaaS, landing pages) across React, Tailwind, Vue, Next, Nuxt, and Laravel. /craft-layer:craft runs the studio pipeline end to end — creative direction, design research, asset sourcing with a licence gate, theming and component build via ui-ux, and a tiered motion system (Framer, anime.js, Three.js/R3F, Lottie/Rive, sprites) with reduced-motion and reduced-bundle fallbacks. /craft-layer:sections guides per-section decisions, /craft-layer:audit reviews a shipped tree, ultra-craft adds web research and a red-team. Ships the Three.js/R3F skill; its review arrives through /code-review:review. Requires ui-ux, which carries the WCAG audit.

plugins.name: design-kit
plugins.description: The Claude Desktop design picker as local, own-your-files skills: /design-kit:slides (an HTML deck; PDF and PPTX by script), /design-kit:design (2-4 artboard directions with knobs), /design-kit:in-codebase (the design rendered with the project's OWN components; handoff-bundle intake with a token-drift table), /design-kit:system (tokens, typefaces and components into design-system/), /design-kit:artifact (a self-contained page, shared on consent), /design-kit:motion (a static design animated into a looping showcase) and /design-kit:film (a beat-synced product film from a brief, with checks by script). One localhost URL under .design-kit/; nothing leaves the machine unless you say yes.

plugins.name: laravel
plugins.description: Laravel best practices: Eloquent N+1 prevention, form requests, service layer, queues, policies, a per-version leverage map (Laravel 11/12/13), mass-assignment security — and the Inertia.js skill (v1/v2/v3, Vue/React/Svelte adapters: partial reloads, deferred props, useForm, shared data, SSR) it pairs with, loaded by the code-review fan-in when the manifests show it — plus the backend-engineer worker (PHP/Laravel) for implementation work; review fix lists go through task-runner's executor or inline, not this worker.

plugins.name: code-architecture
plugins.description: Engineering process: plan-before-code, YAGNI, SOLID principles applied with judgment, task orchestration, work verification — held at Stop by candor's gate (clause 3, refusing a completion claim when files were edited but nothing ran afterward) when candor is installed; without it the rule is prose — low-cognitive-load code, KISS/DRY simplicity principles. Owns structure at both levels: code (units, interfaces, file placement) and system (service boundaries on data ownership, scaling paths, cache placement, sync vs async integration, domain modeling) via the system-design and domain-modeling skills and the system-architect worker.

plugins.name: taskmaster
plugins.description: Idea-to-execution clarification: brainstorm fuzzy ideas into approved designs, grill requirements until zero ambiguity, deliberate the implementation approach with a blind four-persona round (via the approaches plugin when installed; inline 2-3 approaches otherwise), decide visual choices with mockups, validate whole experiences with an interactive clickable demo, then emit milestone-grouped single-prompt task cards. Outputs live under taskmaster-docs/ (no collision with a project's own docs/).

plugins.name: git-workflow
plugins.description: Git workflow discipline: isolated worktrees for feature work, a structured finish protocol for development branches (verify, present options, merge/PR/park, clean up), and review-exchange rigor — what to include when requesting review, and technical verification before implementing received feedback. Ships a PreToolUse guard that refuses any commit, merge, tag or PR carrying a Co-Authored-By: Claude trailer or a Generated-with-Claude-Code line. Includes /git-workflow:finish.

plugins.name: debugging
plugins.description: Systematic debugging: root cause before any fix — reproduce first, read the actual error, isolate with hypothesis tests and bisection, one change at a time, verify against the original symptom; escalation rule after three failed fixes. Ships a delegatable debugger agent for handing off the long reproduce-bisect investigation. Includes /debugging:debug.

plugins.name: task-runner
plugins.description: Disciplined task execution: one task at a time, scope locked to the task, bounded verify-fix inner loop per task, no drift, no unbounded outer loop. Completion means every check passed with evidence — held at Stop by candor's gate (clause 4) when candor is installed; without it a run can end by narration. Ships the shared task-executor agent — the delegatable 'apply the fixes' sink every review routes to — a PostToolUse scope-lock tripwire, parallel-planning (/task-runner:plan), and the subagent discipline (the orchestration plugin was merged in on 2026-09-14): delegation contracts, verification panels, scripts/dispatch-lint.sh, and the ultra-assess boost hook.

plugins.name: overseer
plugins.description: A program-level product owner for long, multi-session, multi-branch builds. /overseer:start "Build a CRM that manages clients" inventories the project and every installed plugin, asks one clarifying round, writes a milestone roadmap, then delivers each milestone on its own branch by briefing the taskmaster pipeline and task-runner execution with skill-pinned dispatch prompts. An accept script refuses to close a UI milestone until the app was driven in a real browser at three widths with a clean console; headless kinds (audit, library) close on a suite tail plus a captured run log. State under .claude/overseer/ lets /overseer:resume continue in a fresh session.

plugins.name: stack-scan
plugins.description: Know what is installed, keep it healthy, find what to add. /stack-scan:report inventories manifests, lockfiles (composer, npm/yarn/pnpm/bun), runtimes and docker images into a required-vs-installed table with drift, missing locks and EOL majors flagged. /stack-scan:audit runs the composer/npm vulnerability, outdated and licence checks — report-only. /stack-scan:suggest suggests every marketplace plugin in three tiers with cited evidence (--yes auto-installs tiers 1-2, --full the stack-relevant set after one confirm, --persist/--global set scope, --sync per project); --skills searches skills.sh for third-party skills — explicit picks only. Add-at-all is approaches' build-vs-buy.

plugins.name: testing
plugins.description: Testing best practices: test pyramid and what to actually test, Pest/PHPUnit and Vitest/Jest idioms, Playwright/Dusk e2e discipline, factories and fixtures, mocking boundaries, flaky-test causes, coverage traps — plus the TDD workflow (red-green-refactor, red-green regression proof for bug fixes). Includes /testing:flake-hunt and a test-engineer worker agent; the test rubric reaches any diff through /code-review:review.

plugins.name: security
plugins.description: Security for web apps: OWASP-aligned code review (injection, XSS, CSRF, authz vs authn, mass assignment, uploads, secrets, dependency audit) mapped to PHP/Laravel and JS/Vue, PLUS design-phase threat-modeling (STRIDE, trust boundaries), a data-privacy (GDPR/CCPA) regulatory lens, and an api-auth lens (token model, OAuth2+PKCE, scopes). Includes /security:review and a security-engineer worker agent.

plugins.name: api-design
plugins.description: APIs in both directions: design your own (resource naming, status-code discipline, pagination/filtering/sorting, versioning, RFC 9457 errors, idempotency, Laravel API Resources, plus a graphql-grpc skill for non-REST surfaces; /api-design:review and spec-first /api-design:scaffold) and consume others' honestly — verify current official API/SDK docs before writing integration code (UserPromptSubmit reminder + /api-design:check, the api-docs-first skill) and keep your own docs true after a change with the docs-upkeep drift scan: README claims, changelog gaps, stale examples, dead links (/api-design:drift).

plugins.name: web-dev
plugins.description: Web development in one plugin: a web-developer worker (routing, REST/API integration, forms, state, SSR/CSR), an opus-floored frontend-reviewer for component and view logic, and three version-pinned stack skills — Next.js (App Router boundaries, opt-in caching, server actions, 14→16), React Native (lists, navigation, native-driver animation, Expo inversions), Vite (VITE_ env security, chunking, base, proxy, 5→8) — loaded by the code-review fan-in from the lockfile. Inertia and Laravel stay in their own plugins; plain JS/TS needs no skill.

plugins.name: devops
plugins.description: Infrastructure in one plugin: CI/CD ordering, container/image hygiene, Kubernetes limits and probes, deploy strategy with rollback, and secrets handling (devops-practices); Dockerfile and compose discipline (docker-best-practices); and local dev environments generated from evidence — manifests, lockfiles, .env DSNs, CI images — via /devops:init (compose-init). One /devops:review loads the Docker skill when a Dockerfile or compose file is in scope, backed by a PreToolUse guard on workflow files and a devops-engineer worker + devops-reviewer pair. Owns infra-layer observability wiring; defers in-code instrumentation to resilience's observability skill.

plugins.name: database
plugins.description: Relational databases in one plugin: the engine-agnostic sql-best-practices skill (sargable predicates, joins, indexes, NULL logic, transactions, keyset pagination, safe migrations, parameterization), the mariadb-best-practices dialect skill (10.6+ divergences, RETURNING, sequences, system-versioned tables, Galera) that the code-review fan-in loads only when the detected engine is MariaDB, a database-engineer worker that applies schema, migration, indexing and pooling work, and a PreToolUse guard that asks before a destructive statement (DROP/TRUNCATE/unqualified DELETE-UPDATE, migration-DSL drops, CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY, NoSQL deleteMany/dropDatabase) lands.

plugins.name: code-review
plugins.description: Stack-agnostic code review: correctness bugs, code smells, convention drift on any diff or PR — severity-sorted one-line findings — plus comment discipline (default: no comment; write-time hooks warn, and deny the strictest patterns, a file over a 0.3:1 comment ceiling and code replaced by a // ... existing code ... placeholder, twice per file each; /code-review:comment-review). Defers structure/YAGNI to code-architecture, security depth to security, stack idioms to the per-framework review plugins. Includes /code-review:review, a code-reviewer agent, the code-smells, reuse-hygiene and comment-discipline skills; the fan-in loads every installed matching stack skill in one pass.

plugins.name: approaches
plugins.description: Solution-approach deliberation before non-trivial implementation: 2-3 structurally different approaches with trade-offs and a kill-trigger, a strategy catalog mapped to the risk each beats, a four-persona blind opinion round for refactor-shaped tasks — plus the merged pre-code disciplines: build-vs-buy checks, rollout planning, design-pattern selection, and /approaches:consult, a blind stronger-model second opinion when a session is stuck or about to do something irreversible (fresh-take merged in). Includes /approaches:compare, /approaches:opinions, /approaches:build-vs-buy, /approaches:rollout, /approaches:pattern.

plugins.name: hindsight
plugins.description: Cross-session self-improvement loop: mines session and subagent transcripts for recurring friction and proposes CLAUDE.md rules, skill/plugin ideas, and defects against the plugin artifact that was running — applied only on approval.

plugins.name: brain
plugins.description: A committed, Obsidian-style codebase map for a project: brain/INDEX.md indexes areas, key files, and notable classes/entrypoints so a fresh Claude session starts oriented. A SessionStart hook injects the compact map (with a staleness hint when it lags HEAD); /brain reads it and /brain index builds/refreshes it. Builds the map only — it never annotates code, and nothing outside brain/ is ever modified.

plugins.name: resilience
plugins.description: Runtime quality in one plugin — does it stay up, can you see it, is it fast. Failure-mode design for integration points (timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breaking, graceful degradation) with the error-handling and concurrency disciplines and the event-driven skill (brokers, outbox, sagas, DLQ); application observability (structured logs with correlation IDs, RED/USE metrics, trace propagation, honest health checks); measure-first performance (N+1, payload, bundle, Core Web Vitals, cache correctness). One audit, /resilience:review, over all six rubrics or one via --concern, and two workers, observability-engineer and performance-engineer, that apply only what a finding proves.

plugins.name: candor
plugins.description: Candour as a mechanism, not a pep talk. One blocking Stop gate, five clauses a script can prove: a file:line citation resolving to no file or past its end; a position retracted after bare pushback with no tool call in between; a completion claim after edits with nothing executed since; a task-runner run stopping without its recorded gate pass; a dependency map changed with an untouched lockfile. Flattery, apologies and defensive phrasing are counted by /candor:check and blocked by nothing, on purpose. Plus the terse reply mode (/candor:level lite|full|ultra|off): chat-message brevity as a shape contract — prose-line budgets and a fixed report skeleton, never less work in the turn.

plugins.name: ask-ledger
plugins.description: Catches the silent avert — work that quietly does less than the ask named, with no reason written anywhere. On the first work-shaped prompt a hook destructures the ask into its named things (proper nouns, quoted terms, 2D/3D-style tokens) and keeps them as a session ledger; a Stop gate refuses a final message that does not account for each one — `<name>: as named | substituted → what, why | omitted → why`. The script proves the accounting exists; whether it is true is the model's word and the reader's eye. Off with CC_ASK_LEDGER=off.

plugins.name: skill-router
plugins.description: File-aware skill auto-routing: a PostToolUse hook injects one additionalContext directive to load the relevant best-practice skill(s) when you edit a matching file (PHP/Laravel/Blade, React/Vue/Inertia via .tsx/.jsx/.vue, plain .ts/.js/.py/.go/.rb/.rs, SQL and migrations (one engine-agnostic rubric, plus a MariaDB row where that engine is detected), components, tests, Dockerfiles, OpenAPI), a SessionStart hook primes a repo-tailored skill index, and low-confidence content signals flush as one digest on your next prompt (SessionEnd keeps the ledger). At most two per edit, named plugin:skill; fail-open, once per skill per session.

plugins.name: command-guard
plugins.description: Destructive-command prevention: a PreToolUse hook that classifies every Bash (and MCP shell/SQL) command before it runs — denying irreversible data loss (migrate:fresh, DROP DATABASE, rm -rf /, docker compose down -v, terraform destroy, cloud deletes, overwriting a live .env, a cd into a missing dir) and prompting on scoped-but-destructive ones (git reset --hard, rm -rf on a path git cannot restore, kubectl delete pod). Reads through quotes, wrappers and heredocs; skips read-only commands. A second PreToolUse config-guard asks before a write weakens settings, hooks, manifests or lint/test config. Ships /command-guard:check and a user-owned allow-file guarded from agent writes.

plugins.name: secret-scanning
plugins.description: Secret-leak prevention: a PreToolUse hook that blocks a Write/Edit, or a Bash heredoc/echo written to a file, introducing a high-confidence secret (cloud keys, private-key blocks, provider tokens, assigned secret literals) before it reaches disk, plus a /secret-scanning:scan command to sweep a path or diff on demand. Fail-open, high-confidence-only, with a fixture escape and CC_SECRET_SCAN=off. A PostToolUse unicode-scan warns on invisible and bidi characters (zero-width, U+202A-E, tag block) in text just written or read.

plugins.name: ultra-deep-research
plugins.description: Deep-research harness that fans out parallel web searches, tiers sources by provenance, extracts date-stamped claims, and adversarially refutes them before synthesizing a cited report with a contradiction ledger and per-section confidence. Trigger 'ultra-deep-research' escalates to a Workflow-driven loop-until-dry fan-out with multi-vote refutation panels; standard depth runs a portable parallel-Agent fan-out. Ships /ultra-deep-research:research plus researcher and verifier subagents. Hand it a contract, RFP, standard, filing or long PDF and it swaps corroboration for coverage of that local corpus. Writes the report inline and to research/<topic>-<date>.md.

plugins.name: toolchain-experts
plugins.description: Five expert reviewers that RUN the project's own static analysis instead of reciting a best-practice checklist: php-expert (phpstan, psalm, phpcs, rector), ts-expert (tsc, eslint, biome, oxlint), react-expert (the hook rules), vue-expert (vue-tsc, eslint-plugin-vue) and ui-expert (stylelint, pa11y, lighthouse-ci, axe). A detect-analyzers.sh mechanism reports which tool is configured, which one CI actually enforces, what the baseline already forgives and which rules are switched off — so the headline finding is the analyzer's blind spot, which no remembered rubric can produce. Read-only; fixes route to the existing workers.

plugins.name: all-plugins
plugins.description: Installs every leaf plugin of this marketplace but opt-in prompt-coach and the game plugins at one scope (/all-plugins:install asks local or project once when --scope is absent; the script alone defaults to local), with --budget also raises skillListingBudgetFraction in that scope's settings so the whole skill listing is sent instead of overflowing the default budget (~6x at 200k), and undoes both — one script with an exit code (0 done, 1 a plugin failed, 2 marketplace not added), via /all-plugins:install and /all-plugins:uninstall or straight from the marketplace clone. Re-run after marketplace updates. Never picks — that is /stack-scan:suggest.

plugins.name: prompt-coach
plugins.description: A prompt coach for the terminal. At Enter it holds an eligible prompt for up to 5 s while a haiku first pass, and on a flag a standby sonnet or opus, judges whether nobody could act on it, it contradicts an earlier instruction, or it strays from a running task-runner card; only a confidently flagged prompt is dropped, and an animated pixel-art sprite shows your text, the reason and a rewrite, with buttons that fill the prompt box and never submit. Each eligible prompt bills a haiku call (a flagged one a standby call too, at most 10 a session), and /cost shows none of it. Terminal only; needs Claude Code 2.1.291; its own failures always pass the prompt. Off with CC_PROMPT_COACH=off.

plugins.name: session-hud
plugins.description: A zero-setup session HUD for the terminal, as a hooks module: a /hud pane with the context window by category, the compaction point, the 5-hour and 7-day rate-limit windows with reset countdowns and the session's cost and time, opt-in pinned so it comes back after you close it; and richer subagent rows. Opt-in: the same figures on the prompt's hint line and what each turn cost on its closing line, for anyone without a statusLine of their own. Plugins cannot edit your statusLine, so this needs no settings.json edit. Each surface is its own /config option. Terminal only; needs Claude Code 2.1.291.

plugins.name: godot
plugins.description: Godot 4 skills that carry only what a model gets wrong from memory: the 4.3–4.7 inversions (Jolt Physics 3D as the default for new projects since 4.6, the 4.7 GDScript override and packed-array changes, flipped defaults), multiplayer authority, visibility and auth footguns, web-export and C# limits; a headless GDScript test runner that exits non-zero on failure; and a standard-library Python checker for broken res:// paths, uids and scene references. Pairs with gamedev.

plugins.name: unity
plugins.description: Unity 6 (6000.x) traps a model gets wrong from memory — Rigidbody and Find* renames, the Unity 6 torque change, Cinemachine 3 class names, Input System project-wide actions enabling every map, Awaitable cancellation, batch-mode CI builds and build profiles, NavMeshSurface/NavMeshLink — plus a read-only .meta/GUID checker that exits 1 when files were moved, renamed or copied outside the Editor without their .meta.

plugins.name: unreal
plugins.description: Unreal Engine 5 traps a model gets wrong from memory — UE 5.8 Zen Server as the default cooked output store (Saved/Cooked holds only ue.projectstore), the 5.8 Visual Studio/MSVC/Windows SDK/Xcode minimums, Enhanced Input mapping contexts that fail on clients and player-mappable key rebinding through User Settings, headless automation tests, UObjects held from plain C++, and Behavior Tree node memory.

plugins.name: roblox
plugins.description: Roblox Luau skill carrying only what a remembered answer gets wrong: remote throttle and UnreliableRemoteEvent payload limits, the yield race that lets two requests pass one cooldown, DataStore request budgets, storage quota and data-loss footguns, Server Authority (AuthorityMode, BindToSimulation, time(), the 64-attribute cap), PreferredInput, the deprecated collision-group methods, and Studio's MCP server and StudioTestService for verification.

plugins.name: bevy
plugins.description: Bevy (Rust ECS engine) skill carrying only what changed in 0.17–0.20 and still gets written the old way: buffered events renamed to messages, resources stored as entities (IsResource and broad-query panics), On<Add<T>> lifecycle observers, flattened pointer events, set_if_different, Name lifetimes, iter_many results, Mesh2d sprites and weakly ordered built-in sets. Reads Cargo.lock before advising.

plugins.name: defold
plugins.description: Defold skill plus a read-only reference checker. The checker (Python, stdlib only) finds what Bob will fail to resolve: compiled-suffix paths in game.project, quoted /paths inside embedded data, require() modules, case mismatches and library paths. The skill covers the footguns that cost a build or a silent run — Bob's truncated and generated-file errors, JDK 25, a headless engine that keeps running after a Lua error, proxy socket clashes, Remotery port collisions — and a smoke test under timeout.

plugins.name: ebitengine
plugins.description: Ebitengine (Go 2D game engine) advice that changed under the model: the v2.9/v2.10 API renames, pure-Go desktop builds from v2.10, Go 1.24's wasm_exec.js move, audio decoder/player pairing, Windows Steam and mobile footguns, a headless CI and capture recipe, and a stdlib Python checker for deprecated calls and Update/Draw loop misuse.

plugins.name: phaser
plugins.description: Phaser skill carrying only what changed from Phaser 3 to 4 and still gets written the v3 way: preFX/postFX and BitmapMask replaced by filters, setLighting, setTintFill reduced to a console error, Math.TAU corrected from π/2 to 2π, Geom.Point removed, roundPixels off by default, pipelines rewritten as render nodes; plus the scene.launch restart and three Arcade Physics footguns (two-sided collision masks, onFloor on dynamic bodies, drag under acceleration). Reads the lockfile before advising.

plugins.name: pixijs
plugins.description: PixiJS skill carrying only what changed from v7 to v8 and still gets written the v7 way: empty Application constructor plus await app.init, the Ticker passed to ticker callbacks, pointermove firing only over the object, passive default eventMode, Texture.from no longer loading URLs, children only on Containers, shape-first Graphics, cacheAsTexture, Particle-based ParticleContainer, the new Filter constructor; plus v8 footguns: particle bounds, renderer preference, the 8.22 contextmenu event, filter texture coordinates. Reads the lockfile before advising.

plugins.name: gamedev
plugins.description: Engine-agnostic game shipping: Steam release (a SteamPipe build-script validator, the store and review timeline, Content Survey AI disclosure, Steam Cloud and Deck/Machine compatibility) and itch.io release (butler channels, HTML5 limits, jam submissions), plus game asset checks, Yarn Spinner and Ink dialogue scripting, seed-stable procedural generation, and console/PC/handheld text-size and loudness floors. Companion to the engine plugins (Godot, Unity, Unreal, Roblox, Bevy, Defold, Ebitengine, Phaser, PixiJS).
